We need to find a template that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the SN2 reaction: C-N formed and C-Cl broken, halide functional group broken. The target molecule is COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. It likely contains a chlorine? Actually the SMILES does not show Cl. Wait SN2 requires a leaving group like Cl. The molecule may have a Cl attached somewhere? The SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. No Cl. So maybe the retrosynthetic step is to break a C-N bond formed from SN2 where nucleophile attacked a C-Cl to form C-N. So the precursor would be a chlorinated aromatic? Actually SN2 on sp3 carbon, not aromatic. The molecule has a side chain: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the triazine? The Cc3... is a benzyl group attached to the triazine N? The SN2 could be on the benzylic carbon attached to N? The group CN4... is a tertiary amine attached via CH2 to aromatic. That could be formed by SN2 of amine onto benzyl chloride. So the precursor would be benzyl chloride (Cl-CH2-aryl) and amine (N4CC(F)C4). So we need a template that breaks C-N bond and forms C-Cl (reverse SN2). The template likely is something like [#7:1]-[C:2]>>[Cl:3]-[C:2] with nucleophile. Let's search for templates with functional_groups_broken "alkyl halide" and formed "primary amines". Already we got many results but need one that matches our molecule. The first result (reaction_id 1014069) seems to involve a C-N bond broken and C-Cl formed? The mapped_rxn shows product with ...[Cl:27]... and reactant with ...[Cl:27]... Actually the reaction shows a product with Cl and reactant with Cl? Let's inspect: In mapped_rxn of reaction_id 1014069, product side (left of >>) includes ...[Cl:27]... and reactant side (right) includes ...[Cl:27]... Wait mapping: format is "reactants>>products"? Usually mapped_rxn is "reactants>>products". In the entry, mapped_rxn: '[CH3...Cl]>>[CH3...]' The left side includes Cl, right side also includes Cl? Actually left side includes ...[Cl:27]... and right side includes ...[Cl:27]... So maybe not SN2.

We need a template that when applied to our target yields a precursor with a Cl. Use apply_template to test candidate templates. We have template IDs (template_hash). We need template_id (the integer used to search). The search result includes reaction_id, not template_id. The template_id likely equals reaction_id? The prompt says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". So template_id is the integer ID used in search, maybe reaction_id? Probably template_id = reaction_id. We'll need to find which template works.

We can try applying the first template (reaction_id 1014069) to our molecule. Use apply_template.
